steps: Cook the white rice according to package directions.
Pat the salmon dry, season it with salt and dust it lightly with the flour so the tare will cling.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pan and sear the salmon skin-side down for 4 minutes, then flip it and cook 3 minutes more.
Whisk the soy sauce, mirin and sake together, pour the tare into the pan and spoon it over the salmon until it reduces to a glossy glaze.
Cook the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain.
Assemble the bowl with the rice, the glazed salmon and the edamame.

note: Honey 10g -> real teriyaki tare: Mirin 20g + Sake 15g with the existing Soy Sauce 15g (mirin is what makes the 'teri'). Added Flour 5g for the traditional dredge and Vegetable Oil 5g to resolve the phantom 'hot oiled pan'. Dropped White Pepper (Chinese-leaning; teriyaki salmon is salted only). Calories 647 -> ~747 (+15%), protein unchanged.

steps: Cook the white rice and let it cool slightly.
Cut the ahi tuna into 2cm cubes.
Slice the onion very thinly and chop the green onion, then roughly chop the ogo seaweed.
Toss the tuna with the soy sauce, sesame oil, a good pinch of sea salt, the sliced onion, the green onion and the ogo seaweed.
Let the poke rest for 10 minutes so the shoyu marinade soaks in.
Spoon the poke over the rice and serve.

note: Relabelled Hawaiian (poke is an indigenous Hawaiian dish, not Japanese) and rebuilt as shoyu ahi poke. Removed the mainland poke-shop toppings Mango, Avocado, Cucumber, Edamame, the second fish Salmon Fillet, and the Miso Paste marinade that no poke style uses. Added Onion 25g (sweet Maui onion stand-in), Green Onion 10g and Ogo Seaweed 10g (limu) - the defining components it lacked. Ahi 150 -> 200g. Inamona (kukui nut) deliberately omitted under the no-nuts rule; shoyu poke is nut-free by construction. White Rice 50 -> 80g so the six removals don't drop the bowl 37% under its old calories (lands at -23%, inside budget).

steps: Cook the white rice, then fold in the rice vinegar, the sugar and a pinch of salt while it is still warm and let it cool to room temperature as shari.
Cut the ahi tuna into small cubes.
Mix the tuna with the mayonnaise, soy sauce, sesame oil and shichimi togarashi until it is evenly coated.
Assemble the bowl with the seasoned rice, the spicy tuna, the avocado and the cucumber.

note: Relabelled American - spicy tuna is a 1980s US West Coast sushi-bar invention, not Japanese repertoire. Added Mayonnaise 15g, which with chili is what actually defines spicy tuna and was missing entirely. Chili Flakes (Italian crushed red pepper) -> Shichimi Togarashi. Rice is now seasoned as shari: added Rice Vinegar spice override and Sugar 2g (the sugar was otherwise a phantom in the step). Calories 515 -> ~624 (+21%), fat up ~11g from the mayo.
